        Anthony Hernandez is a laid-back dude. Nicknamed "Fluffy," the California native is a family man and a stoner. Heading into UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Sacramento, the typically mellow fighter has an intensity to him usually reserved for the Octagon."I'm sober, I'm tired, and I'm not going to lie, I really want to f---ing hurt somebody," Hernandez told CBS Sports on Tuesday.It won't take long for him to get that chance. Hernandez headlines UFC Fight Night in Sacramento, a stone's throw from his home in El Dorado Hills, against Gregory Rodrigues. "Robocop" is a knockout machine programmed with a lifetime of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu data. He won't shy away from Hernandez, whose style is predicated on overloading and breaking down opponents with a relentless pace.Like Hernandez told UFC commentator Brendan Fitzgerald earlier this week: "My goal is to drown you and make you hate your f---ing life."

Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!"Wrestling and weighing on people, I think that alone will slow him down," Hernandez told CBS Sports about his approach against Rodrigues. "He's a heavy, dangerous hard hitter. I think slowing him down would be the smartest way to victory." Hernandez is raring to go. You can hear it in his voice and read it in his body language. It's unusual for him, but not surprising considering how much is riding on Saturday's fight.
The middleweight title picture is difficult to break into. Hernandez won eight consecutive fights before landing his first championship-level opponent. Fellow middleweight Brendan Allen has nearly 20 UFC fights under his belt, yet often struggles to nail down elite opponents. 
After piecing together an impressive win streak over five years, "Fluffy" finally secured a life-changing fight: a main event against then-former middleweight champion Sean Strickland. A win over arguably the division's biggest star could've earned him a title shot. After all, among the darkhorse contenders, many believed Hernandez was best equipped to meet the seemingly insurmountable threat posed by Khamzat Chimaev, the middleweight champion at the time. Hernandez's skill commanded such respect that he was a betting favorite against Strickland. The fight played out much differently. Strickland bullied Hernandez, outstriking him in every round and crumpling him in the third. It was unequivocally a major setback. He went from mixing it up with the very best to having his spot threatened by a KO artist bubbling beneath the top 10 in a six-month span. Hernandez is foaming at the mouth, but insists he isn't lingering on the loss.
"He's really good. It's a game of inches," Hernandez said. "You fight the best in the  world. If you f--- up, he'll exploit you. It's as simple as that."I've been fighting forever. You win some, you lose some, unfortunately. I don't think about it too much. I'm not going to let shit drag me  down. I have way too much going on in my life to think, 'Oh no, I messed  up my opportunity. Shit happens. I'm getting back to work, and I'm  going to make it happen. It's as simple as that. Nobody gives a f---  about you in this world but you."Strickland snatched everything from Hernandez, converting the win into another title shot. Hernandez didn't let it bruise his ego. He accepted an invitation to help Strickland prepare for UFC 328. It was a successful endeavor, with Strickland upsetting Chimaev to capture his second UFC title. Now it's Hernandez's turn to reap the benefits of training alongside Strickland and company.
"I trained with him a lot. It was great, man. He's really cool," Hernandez said. "He helped me adjust some things. The whole Xtreme Couture crew is absolutely amazing. They were nothing but respectful. Nobody was trying to hurt me. Everyone was trying to f--- me up, but no one was trying to hurt me. It was a great experience, and I look forward to coming back." Hernandez isn't treating Saturday like a referendum on his career. He lost and got right back to work with the man who beat him. But "Fluffy" clearly has more bite to him this week. Back home near Sacramento, he finally gets to take his frustration out on someone as he begins another climb towards the middleweight title.Who wins Hernandez vs. Rodrigues, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

title: DeMar DeRozan signing with Nuggets: How does he fit with Nikola Jokić, Jamal Murray? - CBS Sports
description: Denver is coming off a first-round playoff exit and hoping to keep pace in a competitive Western Conference
body:
Denver is coming off a first-round playoff exit and hoping to keep pace in a competitive Western Conference
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        DeMar DeRozan will play his 18th NBA season with the Denver Nuggets after agreeing to a one-year, minimum deal, per multiple reports. The veteran wing will join Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray in Denver to help fill the void at forward after the Nuggets dealt restricted free agent Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a sign-and-trade earlier this week. DeRozan, 37, played the last two seasons with the Sacramento Kings, averaging 20.3 points, 4.3 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game on 48.6/32.5/86.2 shooting splits. The Kings waived DeRozan earlier this offseason, making him a free agent. The Nuggets, coming off a first-round playoff exit, will hope that DeRozan, Cameron Johnson and Aaron Gordon can provide a strong wing rotation between Jokić and Murray.DeRozan will provide them with another scoring option and on-ball creator on the roster, but the fit with this particular Nuggets core isn't the cleanest on paper.  
For one, DeRozan's weakness as an offensive player has always been his 3-point shooting, and Denver's offense has leaned heavily on its wings to provide space on the perimeter for the Jokić-Murray two-man game to thrive. Watson shot 41.1% on 3s last year. DeRozan shot 32.5% from beyond the arc, but the majority of his shots came from the midrange. 
        
            
                The Nuggets are daring Nikola Jokić to leave after a listless summer
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
From there, Denver's offense is heavily predicated on Jokić's creation abilities and the rest of the offense following his lead. DeRozan did play more off the ball in Sacramento, but still self-created more than 61% of his 2-point baskets with the Kings. Watson, on the other hand, was assisted on 65.2% of his 2-point baskets last season, and how the Nuggets balance the contrasting styles will be fascinating to watch. The optimistic view is that DeRozan can help helm the bench unit that has long been an Achilles heel of the Nuggets during Jokić's tenure. DeRozan's abilities as a tough shotmaker might not be ideal in Jokić-led lineups, where the Nuggets can create better opportunities than DeRozan's typical shot diet. But when the three-time MVP is off the floor, DeRozan becomes far more valuable. 
How coach David Adelman deploys DeRozan in the rotation and how well DeRozan adapts to playing alongside Jokić will determine the level of success Denver can have in 2026-27. Gordon is a prime example of a player who embraced the positives of a smaller creative role alongside Jokić and has thrived, but not everyone is capable of making that adjustment, particularly a player who has had as much individual success as DeRozan. Nuggets fans are already a bit on edge about how the franchise is handling roster building during Jokić's prime years, with the Watson trade raising concerns about their commitment to fully investing in trying to win another championship with arguably the league's best player. DeRozan will, fairly or not, bear some of the weight of expectations to help keep Denver in the contender tier in the West with the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder, even on a minimum contract.

Russell, the second-ranked quarterback in his recruiting class, beat out Austin Mack for the top spot at Alabama

        Alabama's quarterback competition is over, and the keys to the Crimson Tide offense belong to Keelon Russell. Third-year coach Kalen DeBoer is expected to name Russell as its starting quarterback, sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz on Saturday. The decision to go with Russell over Austin Mack gives Alabama one of college football's most intriguing young quarterbacks, with the possibility to emerge nationally in the SEC.Alabama's hoping Russell -- the program's highest-rated quarterback signee, surpassing Bryce Young -- will inject a different dimension into an offense that's replacing several key pieces. Offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said earlier this week Alabama's coaching staff was "close" to making the call between Russell and Mack, keeping the timeline consistent with what DeBoer has stressed throughout the offseason -- an expected decision coming after the team's second fall camp scrimmage.Russell delivered from a consistency and operational standpoint, showing he can handle the system's controls during his second season. Russell's dual-threat ability changes the math for opposing defenses. He can extend plays outside the pocket, punish man coverage with his legs and create explosive opportunities when protection breaks down.
For Mack, it comes as a disappointing end to a competition that extended from spring practice through fall camp. The senior and former Washington transfer played in four games last fall as Ty Simpson's backup and is entering his third year at Alabama and fourth overall with DeBoer.Russell does not need to become a finished product immediately, and there will be growing pains, of course. Russell has yet to navigate the pressure that accompanies starting at Alabama, where every decision is dissected, and championship expectations never disappear. But his upside is immense, and DeBoer's track record with quarterbacks suggests the former five-star prospect will be placed in advantageous situations.
        
            
                College football's biggest spending surprises: Why Alabama, Texas Tech and Indiana missed the top 12
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Russell played in two games as a freshman, completing 11 of 15 passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns. Most of his production came against Eastern Illinois, when he was named an offensive player of the week by Alabama's coaches for his efforts.
A former national Gatorade Player of the Year at Texas power Duncanville High School in the 2025 cycle, Russell won consecutive state titles at the prep level and tallied more than 90 total touchdowns over his final two seasons.Russell's not the only new starter on Alabama's offense. Four holes have been filled up front, and DeBoer expects toughness to return to the Crimson Tide's running game this fall while this unit tries to establish its identity. What the Crimson Tide needs is a confident distributor capable of turning broken plays into chunk gains and keeping defenses honest on money downs.  This is part of what makes this quarterback decision so intriguing in Tuscaloosa -- Russell offers exactly that. 
His selection represents more than a depth-chart decision. It signals Alabama is betting on athleticism, creativity and long-term upside at the most important position on the field.

title: College football returning production 2026: What does every roster actually look like this season? - CBS Sports
description: We break down the numbers of which teams have the most firepower coming back this season
body:
We break down the numbers of which teams have the most firepower coming back this season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:33 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football roster building was supposed to get a little easier this offseason. Instead, it somehow got way more complicated than anyone could have predicted.There was no spring transfer portal window this year, only a condensed winter window that still saw a record number of entries. Teams were forced to address major roster needs, departures and additions in a matter of weeks.Then came the five-for-five eligibility rule. Then the federal court injunction in Colorado that opened another path for members of the 2022 recruiting class to return for an additional season. That created another wave of roster movement just weeks before the start of the season, with some programs bringing back players who otherwise would have exhausted their eligibility.And now, apparently, we're still not done.On Wednesday, a Louisiana judge granted a temporary restraining order to 16 football players, including several who had already signed NFL contracts, clearing a potential path for them to return to college football.
For the coaches and front office personnel actually responsible for building these rosters, it's been a summer-long headache. For those of us trying to keep track of all of it, it's been inconvenient.Our process started as teams finished their 2025 seasons, when we began tracking not only returning starters but every player coming and going from all 138 FBS programs (welcome to the club, North Dakota State and Sacramento State) while keeping tabs on how much playing time each roster was gaining or losing using snap count data from TruMedia.We published our initial round of returning production features earlier this offseason using spring rosters as the baseline. But with the eligibility rulings and other roster movement continuing well into August, we went back through all 138 rosters one more time before fall camp to provide the most up-to-date look possible.
All that work produced three different ways of answering the same question: What does each FBS roster actually look like entering the 2026 season?Returning starters are the simplest way to measure continuity, but the transfer portal has made that number less definitive than it once was. Returning snap rates tell us how much of last year's actual workload remains. And career experience shows us how much proven college football a team has on its roster, regardless of whether that experience was developed internally or imported through the transfer portal.Those numbers often overlap, but they also tell very different stories.Here's what stood out.Returning starters: Which teams bring back the most?
        
            
                College football returning production 2026: Returning starters for every FBS team
                
                    Cody Nagel                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The most obvious takeaway from the returning starters study is that the traditional measure of continuity hasn't become irrelevant. It has just become easier to manipulate.
The teams with the most returning starters naturally have some of the strongest continuity entering the season. Georgia, Notre Dame and Oregon each bring back 14 starters, while USC leads the FBS with 15. Six of the eight teams with the best national championship odds return at least 11 starters.But Indiana is the reason the metric needs some context.The Hoosiers became the first national champion in nine years to win the title without returning at least 11 starters, bringing back only eight players who had made six or more starts the previous season. Miami had the same number. Both programs supplemented those returning cores with experienced transfers and immediately played for the national championship.That is the modern version of roster building. You don't necessarily have to keep your players if you can replace them with players who have already done the job somewhere else.
So returning starters remain a useful baseline for continuity. They just don't tell us about the whole roster.Returning snaps: How much of last year's team actually remains?
        
            
                College football returning snap percentages 2026: Production back from last season for every team
                
                    Cody Nagel                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
This is where the roster picture gets a little more complicated. Returning starters can tell us how many familiar names are back, but they don't capture how much of last year's team is actually returning.Notre Dame leads the FBS by bringing back 66% of its offensive and defensive snaps from 2025. Six of the eight teams with the best national championship odds rank inside the top 25 in returning snaps. Indiana and Miami are the exceptions. The two teams that played for last year's national championship return just 44% and 46% of their snaps, respectively.
Coaching turnover is a common thread near the bottom: 21 of the 32 teams with the lowest overall returning snap rates also made a change at head coach. But there are some notable exceptions. Colorado, San Jose State and West Virginia all rank in the bottom 12 nationally in returning snap rates despite keeping their head coaches, while Florida, Michigan, Stanford and Virginia Tech all rank among the top 30 despite changing coaches.A team can bring back several starters and still have a lot of turnover around them, while another can lose a starter or two but retain a significant portion of the players who made up its rotation.The two measures generally move together. All but five of the 30 teams returning at least 11 starters also rank in the top 30 in returning snaps. But looking at both gives us a better idea of just how much of last year's roster is actually still around.
Experience: Which teams have the most career snaps?
        
            
                College football's most experienced teams: Ranking all 138 FBS rosters ahead of the 2026 season
                
                    Cody Nagel                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Here's where the transfer portal has fundamentally changed how we should evaluate rosters.Oklahoma State returns just 11% of its snaps from last season, 133rd nationally. But it also ranks second in the country in total career FBS snaps. Eric Morris tore down much of the 1-11 roster he inherited and replaced a significant amount of that lost experience through the transfer portal. Virginia took that approach to an even greater extreme, leading the FBS in total career snaps, games played and starts after importing a massive amount of proven college experience.
That's the clearest example of how roster building has changed. Five years ago, an experienced team was usually one that had recruited well and kept its players around long enough to become veterans. Now, a team can lose most of its roster in one offseason and replace that experience almost immediately.Returning starters tell us which familiar faces remain. Returning snaps tell us how much of the team stayed. Experience tells us who is on the team now and how much college football they've already played.

title: Hull City stun Manchester United with dramatic opening day upset at MKM Stadium - CBS Sports
description: The Tigers shocked Manchester United with a 2-0 victory to open the season, raising immediate defensive questions
body:
The Tigers shocked Manchester United with a 2-0 victory to open the season, raising immediate defensive questions about Michael Carrick's side
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:42 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It has been 10 years since Hull City have been able to open the Premier League season at home, but the result was the same as last time. The Tigers have shocked one of the big boys of the Premier League, defeating Manchester United 2-0 to open a campaign where most are tipping them for relegation, while Manchester United are a side expected to make a Champions League and perhaps push for the title in their first full season under Michael Carrick.Long-time set-piece specialist Robert Snodgrass may no longer be lurking at MKM Stadium, but the Tigers were able to make the most of dead ball opportunities to score both of their goals as the entire Premier League leans into making the most of these situations. It's easier with a body like Ollie McBurnie to aim for in the middle, and the benefit of scoring in the 17th minute allowed Hull City to put everyone behind the ball and United didn't make them pay for it. And when I say everyone, I mean literally everyone, even McBurnie was essentially playing as a midfielder during the match, and wingers Elliot Straud and Mohamed Belloumi were defending for their lives, recognizing, even on opening day. that any points that the Tigers can pick up inch them closer to the magic 40-point target of safety. The first week of Premier League action is one fit for overreaction, which is why it's good to determine if this game means anything in the long run. For Hull, considering that they struggled at set plays in the championship last seaosn, it's certianly good to see them make the most of thsoe situations but United also allowed 14 goals from dea ball situations (excluding penalties) last season, so it's not as much that the Tigers have improved as it is that they've met a team who can't stop the ball from going in when this happens. You'd hope that this would be something that Carrick would have worked on during the preseason because it could be part of the Red Devils' undoing. Last season, they didn't have European soccer to worry about when determining who the best squad was to play, but back in Champions League play this season, the squad depth will be tested, and the left wing may already be a cause for concern. Patrick Dorgu started the match on the wing before being replaced by Marcus Rashford following his return from loan at Barcelona, but when looking at the choices elsewhere in the squad, it's fair to question how those two were the only options, as they struggled to make a difference in the match while Bruno Fernandes wasn't able to pick out players to make things happen.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Dorgu did play some wing minutes last season, but his numbers are ones that scream of overperformance as a player who is a solid wing back but a defense-minded winger. That's fine if contributions are coming from elsewhere, but when United needs balance, this isn't where they should be looking for it.Alarm bells should be ringing for United, but they're no different than the bells that should've already been there. When teams take the game to the Red Devils, they've been able to hit back, but as they look to rise back to the top of the Premier League, needing to make something out of nothing will be critical. With Ipswich Town up next, United will have another crack at a newly promoted side before getting back to facing the Premier League regulars, and much will need to change. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            They had 71% possession during the game but still had to settle for taking six of their 21 shots from outside the box due to frustration with the Hull City defense. With only three chances that registered more than a .2 xG during the game, the Red Devils created nothing, with the majority of chances coming from Luke Shaw and Rashford after Fernandes just broke the Premier League assist record last season. 
On one hand, you'd expect the real United to be somewhere between this performance and last season, but on the other, a few poor performances like this one could be hard to bounce back from in a league where the soccer waits for no one, especially when expectations are high, like the ones that the Red Devils face. For now, this result is concerning, but it isn't something that signals anything different than we've already seen from United; if set-piece defense isn't cleaned up soon, it could sink their ship quickly.

title: Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz shine together as Arsenal open Premier League title defense with dominant win - CBS Sports
description: Goals from Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, and Martin Odegaard powered the Gunners to a dominant season-opening victory
body:
Goals from Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, and Martin Odegaard powered the Gunners to a dominant season-opening victory over Coventry City
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's the first game of this season, but a team can't show why they're the favorites to win the Premier League without coming out of the gates strong, and Arsenal did just that, defeating Coventry City 3-0. Getting out to a 2-0 lead by halftime thanks to goals from Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz. Martin Odegaard would add another goal in the second half to get to the final margin of victory, kicking off the season on the right foot.It was a lineup that included Saka, Havertz, and Martin Odegaard, something that was rarely seen together last season. In fact, with Havertz starting the season with an injury and Saka ending the season with one, they only started together four times in all competitions, a number that Mikel Arteta will want to see rise in the new season, and the stats facing Coventry are a good reason why. Arsenal were still a strong defensive side, not allowing a shot on goal until the 86th minute of play when Jack Rudoni tested David Raya with a speculative effort, but they were dynamic in attack, playing on the front foot from the first minute straight through to the final whistle. A lot of that was the old guard of the Gunners, but new signing Christos Tzolis also continues to push to make the left wing his own. Starting over Noni Madueke and Gabriel Martinelli after a two-assist showing in the Community Shield.With two shots within the first 10 minutes of play, he showed his ability to get into space and was also credited with a fantasy assist on Saka's goal after his cross was pushed into Saka's path by the keeper. While it's early, these are the kinds of things that he was added from Club Brugge for. Arsenal were interested in Vinicius Junior during the summer, and while Tzolis will not be confused with the Brazilian, they were looking for an upgrade at left wing in the worst way. If Tzolis adapts to life in England quickly it will be a huge boon for the Gunners' title defense.
The Premier League is quite a step up from playing in Belgium for Club Brugge, but Tzolis was involved in 51 goals last season, including eight in Champions League play. Even if you factor in regression coming to a tougher league, this is a player who has something to bring to the squad. It's always good to get off to a good start, and so far, so good for both Tzolis and Arsenal.Despite not having Jurrien Timber and William Saliba in the XI as both deal with injuries, the Gunners picked up right where they left off last season, and it's only going to get better as Bruno Guimaraes is coming to join a midfield that is already a strength for the club, and Ezri Konsa will also add to the defense once that deal is complete with Aston Villa. Manchester City and Liverpool, not to mention Manchester United and Chelsea, will likely have something to say about the title race before it's all said and done, but winning games like this one comprehensively is what will make sure that the Gunners have some room for error.
Winning the games you're supposed to and then not being overpowered in other games when you face top opposition is a route to the title, and facing a newly promoted side, Arsenal did what you would expect. It shows how tough the jump to the Premier League is going to be for the Sky Blues, but after getting this win, it's now all attention to Aston Villa next week in what will be a much tougher match, but for now, Arteta's machine keeps rolling.

title: Nick Chubb, four-time Pro Bowl RB, announces retirement - CBS Sports
description: One of the NFL's most dynamic running backs of the 2020's hangs it up after multiple lower body injuries cut his
body:
One of the NFL's most dynamic running backs of the 2020's hangs it up after multiple lower body injuries cut his career short
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Four-time Pro Bowl running back Nick Chubb called it a career Friday night, announcing his retirement from professional football after eight seasons on Instagram. The 30-year-old began his career with the Cleveland Browns after being drafted 35th overall in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft out of Georgia. Chubb reeled off four consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons from 2019 to 2022, which earned him four consecutive Pro Bowl selections. His best year came in 2022 with a career-high 1,525 yards rushing to go along with a career-high 12 rushing touchdowns. That production earned him second-team All-Pro honors. The 2023 season is when injuries began to rob him of his prime years. He tore both his MCL, meniscus and ACL in 2023 after a gruesome knee injury against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2 that year.  Chubb returned to action in Week 7 of the 2024 season before suffering another season-ending injury in Week 15 that year against the Kansas City Chiefs, this time a foot fracture. He was a shell of himself in 2025 with the Houston Texans after the second, significant lower body injury as he rushed for just 506 yards and 3 touchdowns on 122 carries. That's why he called it quits while remaining a free agent two weeks into the 2026 preseason. "Today's the day I've been avoiding for a while," Chubb wrote. "Twelve-year-old me could never imagine this day, and 30-year-old me is wondering where all the time has gone. I've known for some time now, but I'm finally ready to share that I'm done playing football. I wanted to end my career on a healthy note, along with a winning season, and I was able to do that. At the beginning of this journey, I made many promises to myself. The No. 1 promise I made was that I would always stay true to who I am and forget the things that made me, me. That promise meant always being the hardest-working person, not whether where I was or what the circumstances were."

Chubb's peak of his first five seasons from 2018 to 2022 stands almost without equal in NFL history after he registered 6,341 yards rushing on a 5.2 yards per carry average. He and Pro Football Hall of Famer Jim Brown are the only players in league history with 6,000-plus rushing yards and 5-plus yards per carry in their first five seasons, per CBS Sports Research. Chubb's sixth season in 2023 is when his career-altering knee injury occurred. 
"In the NFL, I wanted to lead the league in rushing, win MVP and win a Super Bowl for the city of Cleveland," Chubb said. "I wasn't able to accomplish any of those things. ... What's most frustrating but also gives me peace is that I know for a fact I gave it my all."

title: Thomas Castellanos enters transfer portal, Texas Tech emerges as possible destination - CBS Sports
description: Castellanos is looking to bring his dual-threat ability back to the college ranks after being granted a fifth yea
body:
Castellanos is looking to bring his dual-threat ability back to the college ranks after being granted a fifth year of eligibility
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After receiving a fifth year of eligibility, former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos has entered the NCAA transfer portal, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.On Friday, a Kentucky judge granted a temporary injunction in an eligibility lawsuit that included Castellanos and former Missouri basketball standout Mark Mitchell. Because Castellanos now has an injunction, he will not be affected by the new ruling in the Colorado lawsuit that took away eligibility for qualified athletes in the class of 2022.A three-star recruit out of Georgia, Castellanos signed with UCF as a member of the 2022 recruiting class. The following season, Castellanos transferred to Boston College, where he started across two seasons before jumping to Florida State as a senior in 2025.Last year, Castellanos completed 58.3% of his passes for 2,760 yards, 15 touchdowns and nine interceptions while also rushing for 557 yards and nine touchdowns. While Castellanos' lone season with the Seminoles was turbulent, he led the team to an upset of No. 8 Alabama in Week 1.Throughout his college career, Castellanos has provided dynamic playmaking with his legs, and he even rushed for 1,113 yards as a sophomore at Boston College. Despite missing spring practice and most of fall camp, Castellanos has already reportedly generated significant interest from at least one Power Four team.
Where will Castellanos land?Texas Tech has emerged as the most likely landing spot for Castellanos as he looks to continue his college career, according to multiple reports. Given how the quarterback situation has evolved in Lubbock throughout the offseason, landing with the Red Raiders makes plenty of sense for Castellanos.Texas Tech paid up to land Cincinnati transfer Brendan Sorsby out of the transfer portal, but due to fallout from a gambling scandal, Sorsby will no longer play for the Red Raiders this fall. Will Hammond — very talented in his own right — is now the starter, but he's coming off a torn ACL he suffered last October.While the Red Raiders are still fine at the top of the quarterback depth chart, the loss of Sorsby made them much shallower. Sophomore Lloyd Jones III is currently set to back up Hammond, but he's attempted just five passes at the college level. Castellanos would give Texas Tech more insurance at the most important position on the field.
That's important because the rest of the Texas Tech roster looks to be a legitimate College Football Playoff threat. The Red Raiders brought in 22 players via the portal, and that class ranked No. 6 nationally, according to 247Sports. Castellanos would help ensure that those title hopes won't be immediately derailed if Hammond is unable to play.

title: NFL preseason Week 2 winners, losers: Bo Nix shines, Fernando Mendoza stumbles - CBS Sports
description: Rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling continues his historic preseason run for San Francisco, while Geno Smith shines
body:
Rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling continues his historic preseason run for San Francisco, while Geno Smith shines in his return to New York
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The second week of the NFL preseason is underway with five games in the books entering the weekend. Preseason football is like a box of chocolates as Forrest Gump would say, "You never know what you're going to get." That's because some squads have their starters chained to the bench, some play minimal snaps and some could receive as much of a half of work. Observing who could emerge as a real contributor from the chaos that is preseason football is tricky given the varying degrees of skill levels on the field all at the same time, but it's possible to identify who maximized their opportunity and who would like a do-over. Let's kick off the weekend by identifying the winners and losers of Week 2 of the 2026 preseason.Winners
                            
    
                                                
                    
    De'Zaun Stribling San Francisco 49ers 2026 second-round pick wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, the rookie 33rd overall pick out of Ole Miss, is THE breakout star of the preseason this year. After catching four of his five targets for 46 yards receiving on Thursday against the Los Angeles Chargers, Stribling is now up to 11 catches for 109 yards receiving on 13 targets. That makes Stribling the first player since at least 2017 to produce at least 11 catches combined within the first 20 minutes of two consecutive preseason games, per CBS Sports Research. Many preseason All-Stars don't end up contributing much outside of special teams for their respective squads, but it's safe to say Stribling will have a place on head coach Kyle Shanahan's play call sheet early this regular season. That's especially true when factoring in how snake-bitten by injury San Francisco is at the position.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    The Houston Texans defenseNo, Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr. and the rest of the starters from the NFL's No. 1 total defense (277.2 total yards per game allowed) in 2025 weren't on the field Thursday night, but the Houston Texans' ferocious tenacity on defense certainly was. They bullied Las Vegas Raiders first overall pick rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the first half, generating an 80-yard pick-six by fourth-round rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz and an 11-yard sack by second-round rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald. 
Seeing McDonald flash pass rush chops like this should send shivers down the spines of offensive coordinators all around the league. If there was an area Houston needed to shore up on their defense, it was defensive tackle, and they were able to do so by drafting McDonald, the 2026 NFL Draft's top defensive tackle prospect in the eyes of many, including yours truly. McDonald, who is listed at 6-foot-3-inches tall while weighing 326 pounds, was more of a run stuffer than a pass rusher in college at Ohio State, but if he can find his groove early on when tasked to get after the quarterback, Houston's defense could be a much greater problem for the rest of the league. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jermod McCoy Tennessee All-SEC cornerback Jermod McCoy profiled as a likely first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft until the medicals surrounding his knee scared teams away. McCoy did suffer a torn ACL in January of 2025, but fears about inflammation and arthritis in his knee caused him to tumble all the way down to being the 101st overall pick and a fourth-round draft choice. In the Raiders' 22-20 preseason victory over the Texans on Thursday, McCoy appeared to be moving well and in phase with opposing wide receivers when tasked with dropping back into man coverage. Perhaps he can end up becoming the best value pick of the 2026 rookie draft class if given the opportunity to receive snaps with Las Vegas' starting defense. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Geno SmithOutside of Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, perhaps no other quarterback had a more depressing 2025 season than Geno Smith. The two-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in both sacks taken (55) and interceptions thrown (17) last season while attempting to pilot then-offensive coordinator Chip Kelly's scheme with the Las Vegas Raiders. Those statistics made Smith just the sixth quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to lead the NFL in both sacks and interceptions in the same season. Kelly had to trudge back down to the college ranks, where he is now Northwestern's offensive coordinator. 
Smith, a second-round pick of the New York Jets in the 2013 NFL Draft, returned to New York after the Jets acquired him and a 2026 seventh-round pick from the Raiders in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick. He kicked off his second stint with the Jets with a perfect drive while leading the Jets' starting lineup on the opening possession against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday before head coach Aaron Glenn decided he'd seen enough from the 35-year-old veteran quarterback to end his night. Smith completed all seven of his throws on New York's opening drive, including the 13-yard scoring strike to tight end Jelani Woods. He also connected with both of the Jets' top wide receivers, Garrett Wilson (one catch on one target for 10 yards) and Adonai Mitchell (two catches on two targets for 29 yards), to finish the night with 65 yards passing. Perhaps Smith's 2025 season was more a product of the overall ineptitude of Kelly's and Pete Caroll's offensive coaching staff. Carroll was given the boot after just one season in Las Vegas, after all. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Jets defenseThe 2025 New York Jets became the first team in NFL history to finish a season with zero interceptions in a regular season. That dry spell unofficially ended in Week 2 of the preseason. Safety Andre Cisco jumped Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard's throw to wide receiver Roman Wilson for the takeaway. 
Jets cornerback Samuel Womack III, a 27-year-old journeyman, generated New York's second takeaway of the night on another interception of Howard. Safe to say New York is an exponentially better ball-hawking group than their 2025 squad. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bo NixThe last time Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix was on a football field, he was fresh off breaking his ankle in an overtime victory over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC divisional round. He returned to action in Week 2 of the preseason and thrived in his two drives, helping generate 10 points for Denver. Nix connected with new No. 1 target Jaylen Waddle up the seam, and the former Miami Dolphins speedster blew by Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney for a gain of 35 yards. That's the big play threat Denver sorely lacked in 2025. 
He then capped the drive by lofting a pinpoint pass to running back RJ Harvey on a wheel route down the right sideline for the 21-yard touchdown toss. Denver head coach Sean Payton ended Nix's night after the Broncos drilled a 53-yard field goal at the conclusion of his second drive, so he finished with 76 yards passing and a touchdown on 6 of 9 passing. Not a bad way to shake the rust off after suffering a broken ankle. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Packers special teamsSpecial teams have been a bugaboo for Green Bay for the last several seasons since the Packers' all-time scoring leader, Mason Crosby, took over as the team's kicker following the conclusion of the 2022 season. The dark days at Green Bay's kicker position might be over thanks to sixth-round rookie Trey Smack. He drilled two 58-yard field goals in the first week of the preseason, one of which didn't count because of a defensive penalty. In Week 2 in Denver, he smacked, pun intended, a 51-yard kick, a 59-yard kick and a 43-yard kick through the uprights, the latter of which occurred as time expired in the first half. Green Bay All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons, who is still recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in Denver last season, is fired up about Smack's performance from the couch.
It wasn't just Smack showing out for the Packers' special teams unit. Veteran wide receiver Skyy Moore took the game's opening kickoff for 30 yards out to the Green Bay 37, and veteran running back Pierre Strong Jr. ripped off a 68-yard kickoff return down to Denver's 32. Looks like Packers new special teams coordinator Cam Achord has found an early groove in Green Bay. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jonathan BrooksBrooks, who was the first running back drafted in the 2024 NFL Draft with the 46th overall pick in the second round by the Carolina Panthers, finally found the end zone in the NFL for the first time. Brooks tore his ACL in his final season at the University of Texas, and he missed the entire 2025 NFL season with another ACL tear he suffered in 2024. He is back in action this preseason, and Brooks was able to shimmy his way into the end zone from a yard out at the Jacksonville Jaguars.   
Losers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Fernando MendozaFirst overall pick, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza had a couple of "Welcome to the NFL" moments on Thursday night against the smashmouth Houston Texans defense, tossing an 80-yard pick-six and taking an 11-yard sack. He finished his night with just 86 yards, and the interception return touchdown thrown while completing 8 of his 15 passes. "It was a play action play, went through my progression, probably should've checked it down to the flat. I saw the flat player get over late to him," Mendoza told reporters when asked about his interception return touchdown thrown. "At that point, I started backing up and threw the check down to Mike Washington. It was not a good throw, we weren't on the same page and it was an interception."  Mendoza did have some nice moments, like a 22-yard dart to Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor in the middle of the field and just in between the Texans' zone defense. He wasn't asked to make a ton of those high-difficulty throws over the middle in college, but they are a staple of head coach Klint Kubiak's Shanahan-tree offense. 
Overall, Mendoza had a tough night at the office despite the occasional flash here and there. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Punter JK ScottSurrendering a punt return touchdown as a punter is never fun, but Los Angeles Chargers punter JK Scott earns a spot on this list for how he allowed San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Jacob Cowing to take his punt back 83 yards for the score. Scott had a chance to make a tackle on Cowing near the 49ers' 45-yard line, but instead of feigning any interest in bringing down San Francisco's return man, he sidesteps out of the way, almost appearing to hold the door open for him. When factoring in Scott will turn 31 years old on Oct. 30 during his ninth NFL season, it's understandable that he made a business decision in the preseason. However, he could have made it just a smidge less obvious, and in doing so, helped prevent a touchdown on special teams. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Will HowardThe 2025 New York Jets became the first squad in NFL history to finish a season with zero interceptions in a regular season. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard, the starter for the home team on Friday, acted as New York's slump buster, tossing not one but two picks the Jets' away on throws intended for wide receiver Roman Wilson over the middle of the field. Not a great way to stay ahead of third-round rookie Drew Allar on the depth chart. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Liam CoenCarolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales gave the NFL world a glimpse of his starters, giving quarterback Bryce Young and his starters two drives on Friday night. Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen didn't meet the moment, keeping quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the rest of his starters in street clothes on the sidelines. Boring.

title: The Nuggets are daring Nikola Jokić to leave after a listless summer - CBS Sports
description: Chances are Jokić -- a free agent next summer -- isn't going anywhere, but Denver isn't doing much to ensure that
body:
Chances are Jokić -- a free agent next summer -- isn't going anywhere, but Denver isn't doing much to ensure that
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NBA's second apron claimed its latest casualty on Wednesday when the Denver Nuggets shipped Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers in an $88 million sign-and-trade that yielded the Nuggets nothing in the way of actual players. They got Cleveland's 2031 first-round pick and Sacramento's 2032 second-round pick, but no Watson replacement. On Friday, they pivoted to DeMar DeRozan. In 2026, Watson to DeRozan is a downgrade. If you believe otherwise, as the kids say, you don't know ball. Getting under the second apron is clearly the Nuggets' priority. They're not alone in this endeavor. The Knicks won last year's championship and immediately let Mitchell Robinson walk after owner James Dolan deemed any trip into the second apron as "suicidal." 
        
            
                Peyton Watson trade grades: Cavaliers grab breakout wing, Nuggets have serious questions around Nikola Jokić
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Robinson went to the Celtics, who have moved off of Jaylen Brown, Jrue Holiday, Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford and Luke Kornet since winning the 2024 title. Oklahoma City won the 2025 championship and just lost Aaron Wiggins, Lu Dort and Isaiah Joe this summer. The Warriors are currently driving their fans insane by playing it so tight to the vest since their 2022 title. The Bucks won in 2021 and have since blown up. All of this is to say, if the second apron has arguably made it easier than ever to put together a contending roster as talent has been spread more equitably across the league (I would argue no fewer than 13 teams will enter this coming season with conference-finals-caliber rosters). It has also made it harder than ever to keep these rosters together for the same reason.
Through this lens, the Nuggets having lost Bruce Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Michael Porter Jr. and, now, Watson from that 2023 title team is no great sin. It pretty much happens to every team, barring some sort of one-off salary advantage like Jalen Brunson giving the Knicks a discount, or Stephen Curry signing a clearance-rack contract in 2012, or the Spurs having Victor Wembanyama (who has since also given San Antonio a long-term discount), Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper all on rookie contracts at the same time. The key, then, lies in the margin replacements. It's an extremely tight needle to thread, but fans look at a team like OKC -- which has nailed everything from adding Alex Caruso and Isaiah Hartenstein to drafting Cason Wallace and developing Ajay Mitchell, which has in turn afforded them the talent cushion to lose a starter in Dort and a two-way wing in Wiggins that every other team in the league would kill for without skipping a beat -- and expect their front offices to follow suit. This is where the Nuggets have fallen short. Again, they never found another 2023 Brown. They didn't want to pay Caldwell-Pope. They tried to swap Porter Jr. for Cam Johnson, thinking they fit the same player archetype, but it turned out Porter Jr. was just way better. Now they lose Watson, their one young, athletic player with the upside to represent at least a plausible path to improvement from last year's first-round-losing team, because they paid Christian Braun $125 million (at least double what he's worth) and couldn't stomach another money dump. 
Problem is, Watson "only" got $22 million annually, which isn't star money. That's regular starter money. Which Watson is, or should be, and being that the Nuggets were already over the second apron and thus crippled by the roster-building restrictions that apply anyway, why not just pay Watson? First of all, that's easy to say when it's not your money. Sure, the Kroenke family is reportedly worth almost $40 billion, but would running your 2026-27 payroll past $400 million -- which would be an NBA record and is what Denver would've been facing had it re-signed Watson at the $88 million he got from the Cavs -- have been a responsible decision for a team that would probably still fall short of true contender status? Probably not. Should they have done it anyway? The answer to that question would be a resounding no if the Nuggets didn't have Nikola Jokić still at the peak of his powers. But they do. And that's where this gets dicey. 
The franchise icon dilemmaWhen you have not just a superstar, but even one step up from that, a true franchise icon, it becomes impossible for fans to accept anything that could be even remotely perceived as organizational passivity, let alone an owner cheaping out. I'm not sure Denver has been passive, necessarily; I would, in fact, largely commend the Nuggets for their commitment to core continuity since the Aaron Gordon trade, which has indisputably served them well. It's also hard to say the owner of a repeater-tax team heading into next season with a nearly $300 million payroll has cheaped out. But yes, the Nuggets have cut some costly corners since the 2023 championship, and they're continuing to do so. No, fans are not going to accept that when their homegrown Hall of Famer is still arguably the greatest player in the world and currently set to become a free agent next summer. That's where having a player of this caliber can, in a weird way, go from a blessing to a curse as every season you're expected to set sail toward a championship even if the boat is starting to sink. It can become a suicide mission if you're not careful. Go ask the Bucks, who mortgaged everything but their soul to try to keep Giannis Antetokounmpo on a team whose window of contention had clearly closed. They waived and stretched Damian Lillard over five years, paying him $113 million to go play for the Blazers, all so they could turn around and pay Myles Turner north of $100 million. They had to trade Giannis anyway, and they'll be digging out from beneath that debt for years. 
That should've been an easy decision. The Bucks were done. The Nuggets are not, or don't have to be, but their margins have become impossibly thin as two younger, better teams in the Spurs and Thunder have risen to West prominence. Watson was a margin call. The guy has only started 64 games in his career. He had one big stretch last season during which his potential materialized, and his two-way upside is obvious, but it's also not unreasonable to not think he's worth an $88 million bet when you're already buried beneath the Braun contract as the only second-apron team in the league and probably not a contender anyway. Frankly, none of the margin calls the Nuggets have made over these last four summers have been unreasonable on their own. Brown was a big loss but the Nuggets couldn't have kept him if they wanted to in 2023 because they didn't have his early Bird rights and were limited in the raise they could offer him. When Indiana threw $45 million over two years at him, short of Brown taking about a $15 million haircut in the first year of his new deal, Denver, through no fault of its own, was out. The $66 million Orlando gave Caldwell-Pope proved pretty quickly to be a ridiculous contract. The Porter/Johnson swap looks bad in hindsight, but, at the time, pretty much everyone was in agreement that Porter was an overpaid third scorer and Johnson, who had just averaged 19 PPG on 39% 3-point shooting in Brooklyn, fit the bill of a similar player for almost half the price. The frustration, to whatever extent it exists, is in the aggregate of all these compromises. In addition to Watson, the Nuggets have also lost Jonas Valanciunas, who was at least somewhat of a plug for the non-Jokić minutes that have crippled Denver for years, and Sixth Man of the Year finalist Tim Hardaway Jr. from last year's team. 
Forgive the fans if the fans if they fail to see the excitement in adding Tyus Jones and Marvin Bagley Jr., and if they're starting, however quietly, to worriedly ponder a question that has always felt like a forgone conclusion. Will Jokić finish his career in Denver?All signs still point to yes. Two months ago, Jokić told Serbian reporters that his "desire is to play the rest of my life in Denver," and that he would "probably [re]sign [with the Nuggets] next year." That probably provides some pause, but Jokić opting not to sign the $278 million contract extension for which he was eligible this summer is very likely a purely financial decision. Next summer he can sign for $359 million. Chances are he will. He hasn't given any indication to the contrary. The concern would be if the Nuggets are taking this fact that Jokic has never threatened to leave for granted, using it as a license to downshift their roster aggression without fear of consequence. This is what has Golden State fans up in arms. No LeBron James team would hoard draft picks and focus on the "next era" because he would be threatening them behind closed doors within an inch of their organizational life. Stephen Curry doesn't do that. He stays in his lane and professes nothing but love and support for all the decisions his ownership and front office make, even if they come at the cost of his last shot at contention. 
Jokic has always appeared to be cut from the same go-along-get-along cloth. But to mistake that for a lack of competitive desire would be, well, a mistake. The idea that Jokic doesn't care about winning, or really even the sport of basketball in comparison to his horses, is rooted in romance rather than reality. It's fun to think about a Hall of Fame player not giving a damn, but it's not true. He wants to win. He wants to do it in Denver. But that's starting to look more and more unlikely as this core ages. You can only play the "if Aaron Gordon could just stay healthy" card for so long. What's funny is Curry's Warriors would be one of the teams that could theoretically pay Jokić next summer if they worked their cap sheet right. No doubt Joe Lacob is dreaming on that as we speak. It's about as likely to happen as the Warriors getting Giannis was. More likely is Jokić stays in Denver as they either fade more and more from contention or pull a rabbit out of the hat to get back into it -- perhaps by trading Jamal Murray or Gordon at the deadline, or even better, by attaching that 2031 Cleveland pick they got in the Watson deal to Braun and/or Johnson's expiring deal for a meaningful upgrade. 
Let's see how it goes. And again, chances are Jokić isn't going anywhere either way. But iI will say this: If ever there was a blueprint for forcing your franchise icon to consider relocation, it would look a lot like a summer in which you allow three significant players to go and replace them with Marvin freaking Bagley. It doesn't mean Jokić is going to leave. I can't state that enough. But until further notice, it sort of feels like the Nuggets are daring him to do so.

title: Inside the fastest show in baseball: What it's like to watch Brewers sensation Jacob Misiorowski - CBS Sports
description: MILWAUKEE – The greatest show on the sand, silt, and clay of the pitcher's mound these days is Milwaukee Brewers right-handed force of n
body:
MILWAUKEE – The greatest show on the sand, silt, and clay of the pitcher's mound these days is Milwaukee Brewers right-handed force of nature Jacob Misiorowski. The 24-year-old is not just the best pitcher in the world in 2026, he's also the most viscerally overwhelming pitcher in the world. Misiorowski on Friday at the Brewers' home yard squared off against Chris Sale, one of the best at his craft and a pitcher some 13 years Misiorowski's senior. It was not only a clash of aces, it was also a duel between two of the best teams in baseball. The 40,130 in attendance -- marking the 16th Milwaukee sell-out of the season (and this one on weekday afternoon) – surely knew it meant a little more than most August games do.  Beyond the importance of the outcome -- Milwaukee won 2-1 -- and what it meant to a Brewers team trying to fend off the Cubs and secure top seed throughout the postseason and a Braves team angling to secure a bye, it was a Misiorowski start. No matter the opponent, that's appointment viewing these days. If you were watching, here's what you saw. First inningWorking from the first base side of the rubber, Misiorowski opens with a 101.8 mph fastball to greet Braves leadoff hitter Ronald Acuña Jr. It's a ball inside. Misiorowski will go to the fastball with all five pitches that Acuña sees -- all triple digits, and four of them out of the zone. Acuña flicks away the only strike, one on the outside sliver of the zone, and works a walk. 
With most starting pitchers, we'd note that they'd now be working from the stretch. Misirowski, though, is unusual among starting pitchers in that he always works from the stretch. Perhaps, with his long levers and maxed-out stuff, keeping it simple is the soundest approach. It's certainly impossible to argue with the results, just as it's impossible to argue with the Brewers' faculties when it comes to pitching development. On Misiorowski's sixth pitch of the game, he finally departs from the fastball and presents Drake Baldwin with a 98-mph cutter. Two offerings later, he goes to the slider for the first time on Friday. It's not his fully gassed-up slider. He's touched 98 with his slider this season, although when his slide-piece is at those levels, it might be more of a cutter than a true slider. If you call it a true slider, then Misiorowski has thrown 49 of the 50 fastest sliders on record. Is a 98-mph slider more impressive than his occasional 104-mph fastball? It might be, if, of course, it's a slider in the genuine sense and not a cutter or the infelicitously named slutter. We know that his fastball is a fastball, though, so it's fine to direct your amazement there, as you likely already were. Misiorowski gets his first strikeout of the game on a 101.6 mph fastball that catches the outside edge at Baldwin's expense. 
Speaking of the typical purpose of pitching from the stretch -- to hold runners -- preventing the steal is a skill of Misiorowski's that gets overlooked. On that note: This was a delayed steal on the part of Acuña, so the out was more an instance of poor decision-making running headlong into William Contreras' powerful throwing arm. Contreras is among the game's best when it comes to controlling the running game, but let's note that Misiorowski has allowed only one stolen base this season – the fewest among qualifiers alongside Ryan Weathers.  Not long after, Misiorowski ends the frame with a backfoot slider to Matt Olson that he whiffs on. He throws the slider about three times as often to right-handed batters, but, as Olson will surely attest, he can back-foot it to left-handed batters as a putaway pitch. This one was 91.8 mph, so, yes, it's a true slider. 
Second inningIt seems like the merest matter of time before Misiorowski eventually authors a no-hitter, but it won't be today. With two out, Mauricio Dubón lines an 0-2 fastball to right for a single. At 103.1 mph, the pitch is Misiorowski's hastiest of the day and the first pitch we've seen enter what's informally known as "Miz Velo Country." It's not particularly fair to throw that hard as a starting pitcher, and what makes it even less fair from the Misiorowski standpoint is how close to the plate he releases the ball. The 6-foot-7 Misiorowski gets, on average, an absurd 7.6 feet of extension off the rubber and toward the plate. That puts him in the 99th percentile in extension among big league hurlers. Take a look at Misiorowski's first inning landing spot, as amateurishly captured from the American Family Field press box: 
And here's how it looked in the fourth inning after Sale has put his spikes on the mound: As you can see, the 6-foot-6 Sale had been planting well behind Misirowski. Sale gets his six-and-a-half feet in extension, on average, and that puts him in the 59th percentile, but thanks to his crossfire delivery he doesn't get down the hill as much as Misiorowski does. That's where the notion of effective velocity comes into play. The hitter obviously has vanishingly little time to react to Misiorowski's fastball, and because he releases the ball so close to the hitter, it's even less time than you might think. Misiorowski this season has averaged 100.6 mph with his fastball, but his average effective velocity -- meaning what the pitch feels like to the hitter -- is 103.1 mph thanks to his elite extension. He has a high leg lift, with the knee basically coming in line with the jersey lettering when he's going into his delivery, and that sets him up to stride deep toward the plate. 
When we talk about Miz's fastball, we'll often couch it in terms like "fastest by a starting pitcher" when talking about Aroldis Chapman in historical terms or Mason Miller on the contemporary front. Miller indeed does best Misiorowski on the radar gun, with an average four-seamer of 101.5 mph. In effective velocity, though, Miller comes in at 102.4 mph because he gets less extension than Misiorowski. Miller may throw harder, but most hitters would probably tell you that Miz seems like he throws hardest of all.  He induced a 2-1 fly-out from Dom Smith to strand Dubón and end the inning. Third inningThe third frame, in which after the first two batters Misiorowski gets into the Atlanta lineup for the second time, sees him take a slider-heavy approach. Of his 11 pitches in the inning, just three are fastballs. He goes to the four-seamer more than 60% of the time overall, which is a point of distinction these days, so this is a brief departure for Misiorowski. Like most teams, the Braves are less effective against breaking stuff than fastballs, and Misiorowski is getting deeper into his secondaries a bit early, since he probably won't go extremely deep into this game even if the zeroes continue to stack up. He's pitching on extra rest, as is custom with him lately, as his workload continues to mount and as the Brewers increasingly operate with a focus on a deep October run. Misiorowski whiffs Austin Riley on a fastball after feeding him three straight sliders. Against the Braves No. 9 hitter, Mike Yastrzemski, he throws a curve for the first time. The curve is actually Miz's best pitch in terms of whiff rate, but this one lands a bit too middle-in, and Yastrzemski lines it to right for a single. First pitch ground-outs to Acuña and Baldwin end the frame. 
Fourth inningFreshly staked to a 2-0 lead, Misirowski benefits from the first ABS challenge of the day by Contreras, who flips a called ball into a called strike at the top of the zone to put Olson in an 0-1 count. He's back to a fastball-heavy approach in this inning and throws three straight balls to Olson before retiring him on back-to-back swinging strikes at the fastball. With a 2-1 count, Harris stings a 99.7 mph high fastball – it's the first hard-hit ball that Misiorowski has permitted on this day – but center fielder Luis Lara makes a nifty ranging catch to prevent extra bases. The 16-pitch perfect frame ends on an Ozzie Albies fly-out. Fifth inningFor a pitcher like Misiorowski, who doesn't throw a sinker and leans so heavily on a four-seamer he likes to spot high in the zone, you wouldn't expect strong groundball tendencies. But Misiorowski has a ground-ball percentage of 45.1, which puts him in the 64th percentile among MLB hurlers. This is because his secondaries all get more grounders than you'd expect given their traits and types. The fifth provides a reminder, and Dubón leads off the inning by grounding out to Brice Turang at second on a Miz cutter. The pitch was at the very top of the zone, but because of the late natural sink it dipped under the barrel and registered a -3 degree launch angle. Another ground ball followed, but this one off the bat of Smith (with a -17 degree launch angle) sneaked into right field for a hit. Facing Riley for the second time, Misiorowski flipped his approach and went fastballs broken up by a slider. He earned a whiff. The Braves brought the potential tying run to the plate when Yastrzemski earned a four-pitch walk -- not a common occurrence for Misiorowski. Yes, his stuff is electricity set on fire, but it's all harnessed and commanded. He's walked just 6% of opposing batters, which is figure that puts him among the league's top control artists (a descriptor that, even so, will never be applied to him). This walk meant Misiorowski would face the perilous Acuña for the third time on Friday in a crucial spot. With a 1-2 count, he fed the former MVP a fastball above the zone followed by a slider at the very bottom of it. One -17 degree launch angle later, a 6-3 putout ended the threat. 
Sixth inningImprobably, Misiorowski this season has permitted a .122/.230/.194 line when facing an opposing lineup for the third time in a start. Still, in-game familiarity benefits the hitter, and the theory holds even when a pitcher like Misiorowski is defying it. The sixth indeed occasioned danger for the Milwaukee ace. To start, he freezes Baldwin for a punchout on the sixth pitch of their encounter. Next was Olson, and Misiorowski got ahead 0-2 thanks to two different brands of sliders – one back door and one back foot. Olson evens the count at 2-2 and then bruises a high fastball, 104.8 mph off the bat, to center. Lara, though, is on the case: The ball off Olson's bat had an expected batting average of .770, but in truth that figure turned out to be .000. Two pitches later, Harris smoked a double to right off a slider, and a mound visit followed. An Albies fly-out put an end to the inning. With a pitch count of 96 Misiorowski's day was probably already done, but the Brewers no doubt noted that against Albies he threw his slowest four-seamer at 97.2 mph and his slowest cutter at 94.7 mph. The Fatigued state is when mechanics go awry, and we know what can happen from there. Wielding the beast of unthinkable velocity means respecting it, at least if you want to keep wielding it. He wasn't his sharpest self in that inning, and, who can say, if the sunlight didn't break through that bank of windows at American Family Field in the sixth and complicate the hitting visuals, maybe it's not a spotless day after all for Misiorowski. 
His final line: 
As of that work, Misiorowski this season has an ERA of 1.68 and an FIP of 2.14 in 145 innings. He's also struck out 216 batters, which comes to a K% of 39.3 -- an absurd figure for any pitcher, let alone a starter who isn't even a quarter-century old yet. All of that -- everything, really -- leads the majors.   The Braves broke through against the Milwaukee bullpen with a run in the eighth and put the tying run on base in the ninth, but in the end the crisp two-hour and 21-minute pitcher's duel -- connoisseur's baseball -- went the way most expected it to. It went to the better team and -- this is often said in reference to a probable future Hall of Famer like Sale -- the better pitcher. The Brewers, thanks to the heavy lifting of Misiorowski, are now the first team to 80 wins in 2026. Given the two moundsmen involved and the two teams involved, it all felt like a prelude to something bigger, say, seven or eight weeks from now. That sounds all right, does it not?

Returning starters remains one of the most commonly cited benchmarks of offseason expectations for college football. While that metric still provides a useful baseline for roster continuity and which programs bring back the most first-team experience, it doesn't capture the role of depth and high-usage contributors outside the starting 11 on offense and defense.Returning snaps helps fill in that gap.It measures what percentage of on-field usage a team retained from one season to the next, capturing both starters and rotational players and offering a more complete picture of continuity.The approach is similar in concept to Bill Connelly's returning production metric, though it is not position-group-weighted and does not account for incoming transfers. Instead, it provides a straightforward look at how much of last season's workload returns from each team's 2025 roster. Overall roster experience with transfer additions can be found here..Using data from TruMedia, our analysis tracks the percentage of returning snaps on offense and defense, with breakdowns by position group and where those numbers rank among the 138 FBS teams. Offensive splits include quarterback, running back, wide receiver, tight end and offensive line, while the defensive side covers the defensive line, linebacker and defensive back groups.
Teams that return most of their offensive line tend to rate well in overall returning snaps, given the position group's high volume of consistent snap participation. A similar effect often shows up in the secondary on defense, where snap distribution is typically more concentrated than along the defensive line.Notre Dame tops the list, returning 66% of its total offensive and defensive snaps from the 2025 season. Six of the eight teams with the best FanDuel Sportsbook odds to win this year's national championship rank inside the top 25 nationally for returning overall snap percentage. UConn11% (127)2% (135)<1% (138)No team in the FBS returns 70% of its snaps across all three defensive position groups. And there are just three teams that hit that threshold in two of the three groups: Air Force, Georgia and Notre Dame.
The Fighting Irish could have one of the best defensive units in the country this season, returning eight starters on that side. And the continuity is spread out, too, with 80% of secondary snaps, 76% of linebacker snaps and 60% of defensive line snaps returning. BYU is the only other program in the FBS that hits the 60% mark across all three position groups.Georgia, meanwhile, brings back the highest percentage of snaps among the FBS' front-seven units. That's particularly notable after the Bulldogs posted a 4.2% sack rate in 2025, their lowest under Kirby Smart and the seventh-worst mark among Power Four teams. With more continuity up front, Georgia has a chance to turn that weakness into a strength in 2026.Air Force leads the FBS in percentage of returning defensive snaps, with its linebacker corps and secondary ranking No. 1 nationally, but the Falcons retained just 24% of their snaps along the defensive line.
At the bottom end, the turnover is stark. Each of the 10 teams with the lowest percentage of returning defensive snaps brings back fewer than 20% across all three position groups. Washington State is the only team in the FBS below 10% in all three, a reflection of the massive overhaul on that side of the ball. More than 20 defensive players transferred out of the program, including a dozen who followed former coach Jimmy Rogers to Iowa State.Why returning snaps still matters for roster buildingReturning snaps aren't a perfect predictor of success, and they're not meant to be treated as one. Teams can and do rebuild quickly; Indiana is the obvious recent reminder that a major overhaul can still turn into immediate success.But those situations are the exception, not the rule.More often, returning snaps help explain why some teams might start faster than others. They don't guarantee wins, but they do point to stability: fewer unknowns in execution, more familiarity on both sides of the ball and a roster that has already logged meaningful game reps together. That kind of continuity tends to shorten the adjustment period in August and September.
Think of it less as a prediction tool and more as a baseline. It doesn't tell you who will break out, but it does help explain who has the cleanest runway to do so. In a sport defined by roster churn, that starting point still matters.
